questionText:
The height $h(t)$ of the tide above mean sea level, in metres, at a coastal location is modelled by $h(t) = 2.5\sin\!\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)$, where $t$ is the number of hours after midnight and $0 \leq t \leq 24$.

(a) State the maximum height of the tide above mean sea level.
(b) Find all values of $t$ at which the tide reaches its maximum height.
(c) Find all values of $t$ at which $h(t) = 1.25$, giving each answer as an exact time.
markingScheme:
(a) Maximum value of $\sin$ is $1$, so maximum height is $2.5\text{ m}$ **(1 mark)**
(b) Solve $\sin(\pi t/6) = 1$: general solution $\pi t/6 = \pi/2 + 2k\pi$, giving $t = 3, 15$ in range **(3 marks)**
(c) Solve $\sin(\pi t/6) = 1/2$: $\pi t/6 = \pi/6 + 2k\pi$ or $5\pi/6 + 2k\pi$, giving $t = 1, 5, 13, 17$ **(4 marks)**

solutionSteps.step: Identify the maximum of the sine function
solutionSteps.explanation: Since $-1 \leq \sin x \leq 1$ for all $x$, the maximum of $2.5\sin(\pi t/6)$ is $2.5 \times 1 = 2.5\text{ m}$.

solutionSteps.step: Find $t$ values where the maximum is reached
solutionSteps.explanation: We need $\sin(\pi t/6) = 1$, so $\pi t/6 = \pi/2 + 2k\pi$ for integer $k$. Therefore $t = 3 + 12k$. Within $0 \leq t \leq 24$, we get $t = 3$ and $t = 15$.
$\sin x = \tfrac{1}{2}$ when $x = \pi/6 + 2k\pi$ or $x = 5\pi/6 + 2k\pi$. Setting $x = \pi t/6$ gives $t = 1 + 12k$ or $t = 5 + 12k$.
